content.text: Building a Claude agent doesn't have to start with a hand-written

loop. Anthropic ships four layers: the Messages API, where you own everything; the SDK's Tool Runner, which runs the loop over your own tools; the Agent SDK, which puts Claude Code's tools and harness in your process; and Managed Agents, where Anthropic also hosts the loop and the sandbox. Pick the layer by asking who should run the loop and where the tools should run.

The platform team wanted a "CI doctor": an agent that reads a failing build's log, searches the repository, and proposes a fix. Two engineers spent three weeks on it, almost none of it on the doctor itself. They wrote the tool loop, JSON schemas for

, path checks so the agent couldn't touch files outside the repo, a cap on iterations, and a fix for the day a long log blew up the context. In review, someone asked why they hadn't used the Agent SDK, which ships those tools, permission rules and context management already.
"Building a Claude agent always means hand-writing the tool loop on the raw Messages API." Experienced engineers believe it for good reasons:

items.text: Every tool-use tutorial starts with the manual loop, because that's how the protocol works.
really is a loop: call the model, run the tools it asks for, repeat until it's done.
Agent frameworks have burned people before, with hidden prompts, opaque retries and painful debugging.
Owning the loop feels like the only way to keep control of approvals, logging and cost.

content.text: The half-truth: you should understand the loop, and sometimes you should own it. But the loop is the small part. The work is in the tools, the permissions, the context that keeps growing and the machine the code runs on, and Anthropic already ships layers that own some or all of that.
Every option is a different answer to two questions: who runs the loop, and where do the tools come from and run? Everything else in the
, from retries to context management, follows from those answers.
With the raw API you send a request, read

blocks, and repeat. You decide every detail, which is exactly why the tool runner's own docs send you here "When you need human-in-the-loop approval, custom logging, or conditional execution". You also own every edge case: results for
endings, thinking blocks that must go back unchanged, and a history that grows with every turn.
Tool Runner: the SDK runs the loop over your tools
The tool runner is a beta helper in all seven client SDKs. In the docs' words, it "handles the agentic loop, error wrapping, and type safety so you don't have to". In Python,
derives each tool's JSON schema from the function's type hints and docstring. When a tool raises, the runner sends the error back to Claude as a tool result with
. You can still iterate over every message, cap the run with
, inspect or modify tool results before they're sent, or take over the history for a turn. What it doesn't have is tools of its own: every tool is a function you wrote, running in your process.
Agent SDK: Claude Code's harness in your process

The Agent SDK, for Python and TypeScript, gives you "the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code". It's a library that runs the Claude Code binary in a process you operate. Built-in tools read, edit and write files, search with
and use the web. Around them you get permission rules, hooks, subagents, MCP servers, sessions you can resume, and limits such as
. If your agent works on files and commands, most of the CI doctor's three weeks is already in the box.
Managed Agents: Anthropic runs the harness and the sandbox

Managed Agents, in beta, is a "pre-built, configurable agent harness that runs in managed infrastructure". You create an agent (model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, skills) once, then start sessions in an environment: an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox or a self-hosted one. Claude runs bash, file and web tools there and streams events back to you. The docs pitch it for tasks "that run for minutes or hours", stateful sessions, and scheduled runs.
The same agent on two layers
For an agent whose tools are your own functions, compare the hand-written loop with the tool runner:

tabs.label: ❌ Wrong
tabs.code:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Why did build 812 fail?"}]
while True:  # loop, schemas, dispatch and error wrapping: all ours
    reply = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=4096,
        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS, messages=messages,  # JSON schemas by hand
    )
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content})
    if reply.stop_reason != "tool_use":  # max_tokens? pause_turn? ours too
        break
    results = []
    for call in [b for b in reply.content if b.type == "tool_use"]:
        try:
            output, failed = HANDLERS[call.name](**call.input), False
        except Exception as err:
            output, failed = str(err), True
        results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": call.id,
                        "content": output, "is_error": failed})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
print(next(b.text for b in reply.content if b.type == "text"))

tabs.label: ✅ Right
tabs.code:
import anthropic
from anthropic import beta_tool

client = anthropic.Anthropic()


@beta_tool
def read_build_log(build_id: int) -> str:
    """Return the last 200 lines of a CI build log.

    Args:
        build_id: The CI build number.
    """
    return fetch_log(build_id)  # an exception becomes an is_error result


runner = client.beta.messages.tool_runner(
    model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=4096, max_iterations=10,
    tools=[read_build_log],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why did build 812 fail?"}],
)
final = runner.until_done()
print(next(b.text for b in final.content if b.type == "text"))

content.text: When the agent needs to read and edit a repository, the Agent SDK brings the tools as well as the loop:

blocks.code:
import asyncio

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query


async def main():
    async for message in query(
        prompt="Build 812 failed. Find the cause in this repo and fix it.",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
            allowed_tools=["Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Edit"],  # built in
            permission_mode="acceptEdits",
            max_turns=30, max_budget_usd=5.0,
        ),
    ):
        if isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
            print(message.subtype)  # success, error_max_turns, ...


asyncio.run(main())

blocks.title: The runner still lets you step in

content.text: Choosing the tool runner doesn't mean giving up control. Inside
gives you the tool results before Claude sees them, so you can stop on an error, and
takes over the history for that turn.

Managed Agents keeps sessions on Anthropic's side: transcripts persist until you delete them, and the docs list it as not eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA coverage. If your data needs either, choose a layer you host.

items.text: An agent is a loop, but the loop is the smallest part of the work.
Choose the layer by who runs the loop and where the tools run.
The tool runner handles the loop for your own tools and still lets you step into any turn.
The Agent SDK gives you Claude Code's tools, permissions and context management in a process you run.
Managed Agents hosts the harness and the sandbox; check its data-retention terms before you rely on it.
